POC is focused on Dedicated evaluation after successful Hosted API demo. Short notes from calls and internal: 
- POC scope: 4 weeks, target start 2026-03-15. Canary: route ~5% prod-like traffic to Redwood Dedicated us-east; monitor for errors/latency/cost.
- Routing/fallback plan: primary -> Dedicated model variant (quantized medium for embeddings, larger high-quality for chat). Fallback -> Redwood Hosted replica in us-west or lower-capacity quantized variant. Region failover: if us-east Dedicated fails health checks for >2m, shift traffic to hosted api in us-west with rolling re-route.
- Rollback policy: auto-rollback to hosted if error rate >2% or p95 latency >2x baseline for >5min. Manual rollback option for SRE.
- Success criteria: p95 latency <150ms for chat tokens, embeddings throughput >=300 qps, cost per 1M tokens within forecasted range.
- Model preferences: prefer open checkpoint (quantized Llama-like for batch embeddings), Redwood-verified high-quality variant for chat. Asked about kernel/quantization profiles and recommended batch sizes.
- Security/Compliance asks: SOC2 report, SSO/SAML integration, KMS for encryption at rest, audit logs ingestion to their SIEM, EU data residency for subset of customers.
- Pricing convo: mid-market discount band discussed; estimate ARR $80k-$200k depending on committed capacity. They want committed vs burst model comparison.
- Quotes from call: "We need predictable unit cost at scale — rolling back if latency spikes isn't an option for customers." — Eng Manager.
- Technical risks: current infra uses private VPC peering; network team needs firewall rules and egress review before Dedicated POC. Also asking for sample load generator / perf harness to run parallel tests.
- Next steps: deliver POC runbook (canary config, healthchecks, metrics to track), provide SOC2 package, draft LOI for reserved capacity, schedule network design review with infra team (Riley to join).
